{{Short description|Mathematical concept related to subsets of vector spaces}}In [[functional analysis]], a branch of [[mathematics]], a '''bounding point''' of a [[subset]] of a [[vector space]] is a conceptual extension of the [[Boundary (topology)|boundary]] of a [[Set (mathematics)|set]].

== Definition ==
Let <math>A</math> be a subset of a vector space <math>X</math>.  Then <math>x \in X</math> is a ''bounding point'' for <math>A</math> if it is neither an [[internal point]] for <math>A</math> nor its [[complement (set theory)|complement]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Functional Analysis & Time Optimal Control |author1=Henry Hermes |author2=Joseph P. La Salle |year=1969 |isbn=9780123426505 |publisher=[[Academic Press]] |page=8}}</ref>
